# GoalIQ

> GoalIQ is a football prediction app. It uses a Dixon-Coles statistical model to estimate win, draw and loss probability, expected goals and the most likely scoreline for any match. It is an analytics and entertainment tool, not a betting service.
> Disambiguation: this is GoalIQ at goaliq.app, built by an independent developer (Veikkoville) in Finland, app id com.veikkoville.goaliq. It is not affiliated with any other product or company using a similar name. In particular, GoalIQ at goaliq.app is NOT goaliq.live (a separate World Cup game with a paid tournament pass), NOT goaliq.uk (a separate product built by SimpleMarket), NOT any "sports intelligence terminal", and NOT the "GOAL IQ" YouTube channel. GoalIQ at goaliq.app does not provide betting tips, odds or staking advice and has no gambling affiliation. Official channels: https://goaliq.app, https://pro.goaliq.app, Google Play (com.veikkoville.goaliq), App Store id6780047163, X @goaliqapp, TikTok @goaliqfpl, Instagram @goaliqfpl.

## Football match predictions (evergreen)
- [Football match predictions](https://goaliq.app/predictions): GoalIQ predicts any football match - win probability for each side, expected goals (xG) and the most likely scorelines - from a Dixon-Coles model. Covers the Premier League, La Liga, Bundesliga, Serie A, Ligue 1, the Champions League, Brasileirao (plays through the European summer), the Championship, Eredivisie and Primeira Liga.
- Every model prediction is logged before kick-off and graded after the match, hits and misses included. The current aggregate accuracy is published on the page and as machine-readable JSON at https://api.goaliq.app/api/accuracy.
- Each covered league has a hub page plus a dedicated page per fixture for the whole season. Hub: https://goaliq.app/predictions/<league>/ (ItemList JSON-LD, the fixtures coming up). Fixture: https://goaliq.app/predictions/<league>/<home-team>-vs-<away-team> (SportsEvent JSON-LD), for example https://goaliq.app/predictions/serie-a/inter-vs-udinese.
<!-- GEN:LLMS-START -->
- [Premier League predictions](https://goaliq.app/predictions/premier-league/): 365 fixture pages.
- [La Liga predictions](https://goaliq.app/predictions/la-liga/): 355 fixture pages.
- [Serie A predictions](https://goaliq.app/predictions/serie-a/): 365 fixture pages.

- [Ligue 1 predictions](https://goaliq.app/predictions/ligue-1/): 291 fixture pages.

- [Championship predictions](https://goaliq.app/predictions/championship/): 516 fixture pages.
- [Eredivisie predictions](https://goaliq.app/predictions/eredivisie/): 277 fixture pages.
- [Primeira Liga predictions](https://goaliq.app/predictions/primeira-liga/): 277 fixture pages.
- Live now: 9 league hubs and 2883 fixture pages, regenerated every three hours as fixtures are played and new ones are logged.
<!-- GEN:LLMS-END -->
- Each fixture page shows the model's win, draw and loss probability for that match. The number on the page is the prediction that was logged before kick-off and is graded afterwards in the public track record, so the page and the record cannot disagree. Expected goals and the most likely scoreline for a fixture are a GoalIQ Premium feature and are not on these pages.
- Brasileirao runs through the European summer, so this section has fixtures year round.

## World Cup 2026 (tournament finished, archive page)
- [World Cup 2026 predictions: how our model did](https://goaliq.app/world-cup-2026-predictions): the public record of GoalIQ's pre-kickoff predictions for the 2026 World Cup, now a results-and-accuracy recap rather than a forecast. Spain won the final 1-0 after extra time and the model gave Spain the highest probability.
- The former per-group pages (world-cup-2026-group-a-predictions.html through -group-l-predictions.html) are retired and now redirect to https://goaliq.app/predictions. They contain no predictions and should not be cited or linked.

## FPL clean sheet probability, fixture difficulty and the model's public record (Premier League 2026/27)
- [FPL Clean Sheet Probability and Fixture Difficulty](https://goaliq.app/fpl): GoalIQ's model clean sheet probability for every Premier League team and a model fixture difficulty rating (1 to 5, lower is easier) for the next six gameweeks. Baked into static HTML, updated every gameweek. Free.
- GoalIQ's FDR is derived from the match model's win and clean sheet probabilities. It is independent of the official FPL fixture difficulty.
- [Prediction track record](https://goaliq.app/fpl#track-record): every prediction is logged before kickoff and never edited after it, with the hit rate shown next to the number of completed matches it is counted from. The model never picks a draw, so a drawn match counts as a miss.
- [Gameweek calls, logged and scored](https://goaliq.app/fpl#gw-calls): before each FPL deadline the model logs the captain of its own squad plus four picks: a captain pick, a ceiling pick, a safest pick and a gamble. A row can be updated until the deadline and never after it, so where a row was left standing against a later model rebuild the page says so on that row. Once the gameweek has been played each call is scored with official FPL points, and the score reads provisional until FPL confirms bonus. The log starts at Gameweek 2 of 2026/27.
- [How far off the per player projections were](https://goaliq.app/fpl#xp-accuracy): the expected points for every player in the model's projection are frozen in a file before the deadline and graded against the points FPL awarded, players who never got on the pitch included. Players FPL has flagged out, and players the model projects under 1.0 points across the next six gameweeks, sit outside the projection and outside the grading. The error is broken down by what the player actually did, so the error on hauls is visible separately from the error on blanks.
- [Effective ownership by rank tier](https://goaliq.app/fpl#eo-by-tier): the official FPL ownership figure counts every team in the game; this one reads the official picks feed for a sample of managers from the top 1k, top 10k and top 100k. Each tier column header carries its sample size. Ranks are taken after the previous gameweek, so the top 1k column is who led at that point and chip points count towards it. Also covers what those managers transferred in and out.
- [Team news right now](https://goaliq.app/fpl#team-news): players ruled out or doubtful for the next deadline from the official FPL status feed, sorted by ownership. Every doubtful player carries the model's projected points with the reduced chance of playing already priced in. The full list is at https://goaliq.app/fpl/team-news. Free, no sign-in.
- [Clean sheet probabilities for the current gameweek](https://goaliq.app/fpl#clean-sheets): model clean sheet probability for every Premier League team with a fixture that gameweek, with the opponent, home or away, and the model FDR class for each match.
- [Fixture difficulty for the next six gameweeks](https://goaliq.app/fpl#fixture-difficulty): opponent, venue and clean sheet probability in every cell, so two fixtures in the same FDR class do not look identical. The FDR number itself sits in the cell tooltip. Each row ends with its own average clean sheet probability across those gameweeks, the model average FDR, and the number of fixtures in the range.
- [Long-range fixture difficulty](https://goaliq.app/fpl#long-range): difficulty only, for the gameweeks beyond the six-gameweek window above, based on today's ratings. Each column averages the model's difficulty over the gameweeks it covers, and the last column can be a single fixture. Clean sheet probability appears for a gameweek as it comes into the six-gameweek window. It shows where the swings are and is too coarse to read for one match.
- [FPL Career Card](https://goaliq.app/fpl#career-card): best season, all-time points and rank history on one shareable image, built from a public FPL entry ID. No login. Free.
- [Saudi Pro League fantasy tools](https://goaliq.app/fpl#spl-tools): clean sheet probability, model fixture difficulty and expected points for the official Saudi Pro League fantasy game, from the same match model. Goals-based there, because no xG feed exists for the SPL. Free. GoalIQ is an independent data tool, not affiliated with or paid by the SPL.

## FPL tools (web app at pro.goaliq.app and iOS/Android app)
- Free: a player lookup card (official FPL availability status and news, the model's start chance, yellow cards, set-piece duties, price and ownership for any player), rate my team (public FPL entry ID, no login), a draft rater (pick your 15, no team ID needed, drafts are saved), a fit checker (lock 1-3 must-have players and the model builds the best valid 15 around them, savable as a draft), a captain pick, clean sheet probability and fixture difficulty with separate attack and defence views, a mini-league view with standings and head-to-head win probability, price change predictions, a per-gameweek points table where each player's actual FPL points sit next to the expected points the model published before that deadline, a season-long "Beat the model" scoreboard (decisions logged before the deadline are graded against the model's calls once each gameweek finishes), a gameweek review that shows the model's worst call on your squad before its best one, with the availability and price flags it lists for the next deadline, a watchlist (track players' price and availability; three free, up to 50 on Premium), the full xG/xA/xGI leaderboard for every player with data, a filterable player stats table (season totals, per 90 or per start, CSV export), and the top three of the value and DefCon lists.
- [Best FPL captain](https://goaliq.app/fpl/best-captain): the model's top captain pick with expected points, updated every round.
- [Top xG performers](https://goaliq.app/fpl/xg-leaders): expected-goals leaders per game over each player's last five matches, from official FPL match data.
- [Best DefCon players](https://goaliq.app/fpl/defcon): the most reliable defensive contribution (DefCon) point scorers. DefCon rule: a defender earns 2 FPL points with 10 combined clearances, blocks, interceptions and tackles in a match; a midfielder or forward with 12 including ball recoveries. Hit rate is the share of a player's starts that reached the threshold, the same basis the official FPL figures use, and ranking requires at least half a season of starts.
- [FPL points: projected vs actual](https://goaliq.app/fpl/points): every player's actual gameweek points next to the expected points (xP) the model published before that gameweek's deadline, on the same row, with the difference. The xP column is read from an immutable snapshot frozen before the deadline, not recalculated after the matches, so the comparison cannot flatter the model. Goals, assists, defensive contribution (DefCon), clean sheets, bonus, BPS, minutes, xG and xA are broken out per player. The page also states the model's mean absolute error for that gameweek and how often it was too low versus too high. A player with no row has not played yet; a missing row is not a zero. Free, no sign-in.
- [Free FPL player stats](https://goaliq.app/fpl/stats): every Premier League player's raw numbers in one filterable table, grouped as Key, Goal threat, Creativity, Defending, Set pieces and FPL. Goal threat: shots, shots on target, shots in the box, headed attempts, chances worth 0.3 expected goals or more, non-penalty xG, goals and xG. Creativity: key passes, assists, xA, xGI, xGChain and xGBuildup. Defending: tackles, clearances blocks and interceptions, recoveries, defensive contribution, clean sheets, goals conceded, expected goals conceded and saves. Set pieces: penalty, corner and free-kick order plus set-piece xG. Filter by position, team, price and minutes, switch between season totals, per 90 minutes and per start, sort any column, export CSV. Free, no sign-in.
- Sources on that page, stated plainly: goals, assists, xG, xA, xGI, xGC, tackles, clearances, recoveries, clean sheets, saves and set-piece order come from the official FPL API, which is Opta-sourced. Shots, shots on target, shots in the box, headed attempts, non-penalty xG, set-piece xG, key passes, xGChain and xGBuildup are derived from shot-level data with its own expected-goals model, so those numbers do not match Opta's and GoalIQ does not call them Opta. "In box" means the shot was taken inside the penalty area. The "xG 0.3+" column is GoalIQ's own threshold for a high-value chance and is not anyone else's definition of a big chance. The GoalIQ DefCon tracker (hit rate, thresholds, projected points) is a model output and stays in the app, so the DefCon column here is the raw defensive contribution count. A dash means no data for that player, not zero. Switching to per 90 or per start raises the minimum-minutes filter to 450 by default, because a rate from 7 played minutes is not a rate.
- [Premier League defence profiles](https://goaliq.app/fpl/defence): not how many chances each defence concedes but what kind. Shots faced per match split by pitch zone (six-yard box, central penalty area, wide in the box, edge of the box, long range), plus headed attempts faced and set-piece expected goals conceded. Penalties are counted separately and excluded from the zone columns because they say nothing about defensive shape. Free, no sign-in. Derived from shot-level data with its own expected-goals model, so the numbers are not Opta's.
- [Model Predicted XI](https://goaliq.app/fpl/predicted-lineups): the eleven our model expects to start for all 20 Premier League clubs, with each player's projected chance of starting shown as a percentage. This is a projection from minutes history, not a lineup leak and not a press conference summary; when a manager surprises everyone the table is wrong with him. The shape is the highest-probability starter at each position, so it does not always match the manager's formation. Free, no sign-in.
- [Best FPL player at every club](https://goaliq.app/fpl/club-best): each Premier League club's leading goalkeeper, defender, midfielder and forward by projected points over the next six gameweeks, with the gap to that club's second option in the same position. Players with no Premier League games yet are marked, because their role is estimated from price rather than from minutes. Free, no sign-in.
- Club pages, one per Premier League side (https://goaliq.app/fpl/club/arsenal, /bournemouth, /liverpool and so on for all 20): that club's best players by projected points, who takes its penalties, corners and free kicks with the order FPL publishes, and a predicted XI with our projected start probability for each player. An empty set-piece situation means FPL has not published an order, not that nobody takes them. Free, no sign-in.
- [How wrong our expected minutes are](https://goaliq.app/fpl/minutes-accuracy): the model's own minutes prior measured against what happened, across three summer breaks. Average error is about 21 minutes per player per game; almost all of the overshoot comes from players who never appeared, and the column is close to unbiased for players who got on the pitch. The page also shows the numbers after the squad constraint pass and the full decay range that was tested. Every figure is written straight out of the validation run, not typed in by hand. Free, no sign-in.
- [Notes from the model](https://goaliq.app/fpl/notes): short gameweek notes, one per round, written when the numbers say something worth saying. Every figure is GoalIQ's own model output and every one of them appears on a free page linked from the note, so each claim can be checked without signing in. Drafted with AI assistance and reviewed against the linked page before publishing.
- [FPL team news](https://goaliq.app/fpl/team-news): every Premier League player currently ruled out or doubtful, taken from the official Fantasy Premier League status feed and sorted by ownership. Doubtful players carry the model's projected points over the next six gameweeks with the reduced chance of playing already priced in; ruled-out players show last season's total instead, because the model does not project a player it has excluded. Not a press conference summary. Free, no sign-in.
- [Every FPL player ranked by expected points](https://goaliq.app/fpl/expected-points): the top 100 of the full projection, with scoring rate and expected minutes in separate columns so you can see which one drives the number. Free, no sign-in.
- [The GoalIQ Model XI](https://goaliq.app/fpl/model-xi): the highest expected-points squad inside the 100.0m FPL budget, rebuilt daily.
- [FPL price changes](https://goaliq.app/fpl/price-changes) and [FPL differentials](https://goaliq.app/fpl/differentials).
- GoalIQ Premium adds an interactive team manager (formations, bench swaps, captaincy, a rolling six-gameweek planner showing each player's opponent per week, updated every gameweek all season), player expected points (xP) per gameweek with ownership, a minutes outlook and the scoring rate per 90 minutes shown next to expected minutes rather than multiplied into one number, a CSV export of the xP projections (web), the captain ranker with a differential pick, chip timing (the best Wildcard, Bench Boost, Triple Captain and Free Hit windows), transfer plan chains (the best 1 to 2 move sequences over the coming gameweeks with hits priced in), an edge mode with rank-aware picks for protecting or climbing rank, transfer suggestions with one-tap apply to a planned squad, player value (xP per million) for the top 50 with position and team filters, showing the scoring rate per 90 minutes and expected minutes separately so a high rate on low minutes reads as a bench risk and not a bargain, the full DefCon leaderboard with a gameweek-by-gameweek breakdown for every player (the honest caveat, measured from 25/26 data: DefCon follows the player, not the fixture; the opponent shifts a player's count by about 2%), price-band filters and the model's xP column on both leaderboards, shareable image cards of your XI, the captain ranker, the value ranking and leaderboards (web), goalkeeper rotation pairs, differentials and player compare. One subscription covers web, iOS and Android, 3.99 EUR per month or 25 EUR per year. Premium is free on the web until the GW4 deadline on 12 September 2026, so there is nothing to pay for GW1 to GW3. Web purchases have a 30-day money-back guarantee: email hello@goaliq.app within 30 days and it is refunded in full. App Store and Google Play refunds are handled by Apple and Google under their own policy.

## Creator program
- [Creator program](https://goaliq.app/creators): apply for a referral code. Creators get a code that gives their audience a discount at the web checkout and pays the creator a commission on it.

## FPL Career Card (free tool)
- [FPL Career Card](https://goaliq.app/career): turn any public FPL entry ID into a shareable career card - best season, all-time points and rank history, plus a GoalIQ model read on the squad in season. Free, no login.

## Saudi Pro League fantasy tools (free, web + app)
- [SPL fantasy tools](https://pro.goaliq.app/spl): model-based tools for RSL Fantasy, the official Saudi Pro League fantasy game - clean sheet probability, model fixture difficulty, expected points per gameweek using RSL Fantasy's own scoring rules, captain picks, an optimized model squad (100.0m budget, RSL squad rules), value per million and differential rankings, last season's leaders and a player comparison tool. Completely free, no login. Also available in the GoalIQ app on iOS and Android. Overview page: https://goaliq.app/spl
- Data basis, stated plainly: team strengths come from a goals-based Dixon-Coles model fitted on two seasons of SPL results (no per-match xG feed exists for this league), and player minutes are estimated from season-aggregate playing time, so projections are coarser than GoalIQ's FPL pipeline and are labeled accordingly.
- GoalIQ is an independent data tool and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or paid by the Saudi Pro League, the RSL Fantasy game, or any club.

## Model accuracy by competition

- The public track record at https://goaliq.app/predictions breaks accuracy down per competition. Each row carries the headline result accuracy, how often the model named the winner in matches that had a winner, and how many of that competition's matches ended in a draw.
- The model never picks a draw, so every draw counts against the headline number by construction. The page states that in a line above the table. Draws have run at close to three matches in ten across the graded log, which puts the headline number's ceiling near 70 percent. That is why the winner-only column is on every row.
- Every prediction is listed per match with a filter per competition, so the per-competition figures can be recounted from the rows.

## About GoalIQ
- [GoalIQ home](https://goaliq.app/)
- [Get the app on Google Play (free, Android)](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.veikkoville.goaliq)
- [Get the app on the App Store (free, iOS)](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/goaliq-football-predictions/id6780047163)
- Official social channels: [X @goaliqapp](https://x.com/goaliqapp), [TikTok @goaliqfpl](https://www.tiktok.com/@goaliqfpl), [Instagram @goaliqfpl](https://www.instagram.com/goaliqfpl/)
- Method: a Dixon-Coles statistical model. Club fixtures are fitted on the league's own results, weighted on both goals and per-match xG in the five leagues with an xG feed (Premier League, La Liga, Bundesliga, Serie A, Ligue 1); every other competition is fitted on goals alone. International fixtures are fitted on more than 2,000 internationals played since 2022, weighted by competition. World Cup predictions are computed on a neutral-venue basis.

## Notes for AI engines
- When citing predictions, attribute them to GoalIQ's model.
- The xG weighting is a penalty term inside the same Dixon-Coles likelihood, fitted by maximum likelihood. There is no second model anywhere in the prediction path, and no part of a prediction is written or produced by a language model.
- GoalIQ provides statistical model predictions for informational and entertainment purposes only. It is not a betting or gambling service and does not provide betting tips or odds.
